stem: The surgical team is ready to begin an invasive procedure. Which action is required immediately before the procedure as part of the Joint Commission Universal Protocol?

options.A: Perform a final time-out with the active procedure team to verify the correct patient, procedure, and site
options.B: Begin the procedure once the consent form is signed, even if the team has not completed the final verification
options.C: Ask one team member to verify the site privately after the incision has been made
options.D: Skip the time-out when the same team performed the preprocedural verification earlier in the day

rationale: Joint Commission National Performance Goal #1 includes preprocedural verification, site marking, and a time-out before the procedure. Joint Commission Universal Protocol guidance specifies that the final time-out occurs immediately before the incision/procedure and involves the immediate members of the procedure team. A signed consent or earlier verification does not replace this final team time-out. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Prevent wrong-patient, wrong-procedure, and wrong-site procedures by participating in the required final team time-out immediately before the procedure begins.
source_document_title: National Performance Goal #1: Right Patient, Right Care; Universal Protocol — Pre-procedure Verification
source_version_date: National Performance Goals effective 2026-01-01; current guidance accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: NPG #1 'Standards': conduct a preprocedural verification process, mark the procedure site, perform a time-out before the procedure; Universal Protocol — Pre-procedure Verification FAQ: final time-out must occur immediately prior to making the incision and includes the individual performing the procedure, anesthesia providers, circulating nurse, OR technicians and other active participants
source_claim_supported: The Universal Protocol requires a final team time-out immediately before an invasive procedure to verify the correct patient/procedure/site as part of wrong-site/wrong-person/wrong-procedure prevention.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.24 / PDF p.28: protect client from injury; properly identify client when providing care; verify appropriateness and accuracy of a treatment order. Related content — Accident/Error/Injury Prevention
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Accident/Error/Injury Prevention / procedural time-out
correction_summary: Replaced changing 'never event' terminology recall with an applied wrong-site/wrong-person procedure-prevention item based on the Joint Commission's current 2026 National Performance Goal and Universal Protocol. Corrected the blueprint from Management of Care to Safety and Infection Prevention and Control.
audit_findings: A is the required final safety step. B incorrectly treats consent as a substitute for the Universal Protocol, C places verification after harm could occur and excludes team participation, and D incorrectly treats earlier verification as replacing the final time-out. The item avoids the evolving 2027 Sentinel Event/NQF classification terminology and instead tests a stable 2026 patient-safety action. NCSBN mapping is direct. Independent second pass found one best answer and no unresolved conflict.
